query: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

## Abstract
In high-entropy materials, local chemical fluctuation from multiple elements inhabiting the same crystallographic site plays a crucial role in their unique properties. Using atomic-resolution chemical mapping, we identified the respective contributions of different element characteristics on the local chemical fluctuation of high-entropy structures in thermoelectric materials. Electronegativity and mass had a comparable influence on the fluctuations of constituent elements, while the radius made a slight contribution. The local chemical fluctuation was further tailored by selecting specific elements to induce large lattice distortion and strong strain fluctuation to lower lattice thermal conductivity independent of increased entropy. The chemical bond fluctuation induced by the electronegativity difference had a noticeable contribution to the composition-dependent lattice thermal conductivity in addition to the known fluctuations of mass and strain field. Our findings provide a fundamental principle for tuning local chemical fluctuation and lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy thermoelectric materials. However, the low performance and conversion efficiency of thermoelectric materials have hindered their realistic applications. As the latest promising approach (, ), the high-entropy strategy has demonstrated substantial improvements in the performance of thermoelectric materials (, , ). The local chemical fluctuation can interrupt the long-range periodic arrangement of atoms and induce the strong scattering of heat-carrying phonons (), which largely reduce the lattice thermal conductivity and improves thermoelectric properties. The vast number of possible element combinations in the high-entropy strategy offers an enormous amount of space to tune local chemical fluctuation. However, altering the composition of high-entropy materials may not always lead to desired properties, and the tailoring of local chemical fluctuations by constituent elements has remained unclear in most of studies.
